profile.entities: Punjab National Bank (10,300 branches); subsidiaries PNB Housing, PNB MetLife, PNB Gilts
profile.mgmt: Ashok Chandra (MD & CEO); M. Paramasivam (ED); Amit Kumar Srivastava (ED); Raman Grover, Sunil Kumar Goyal (CGM). Moderator: Palak Shah, Elara Securities

bull_bear.body: - CRAR 18.13% / CET1 14.52% — large cushion; prudent floating-provision build (INR 390 cr/qtr, INR 2,435 cr total) to pre-fund ECL; IL&FS TN Power ~INR 1,000 cr write-back as a "kitty" for FY27. Subsidiary value-maximisation over stake changes.
bull_bear.title: Capital allocation

bull_bear.body:
- **Monsoon / El Niño:** MD concedes a bad kharif would be "a big challenge" across agri and agri-linked income — the key macro swing (watch Aug-Sep).
- **ECL adoption 1-Apr-27:** INR 9,500-10,000 cr one-time + 10-12 bps/qtr recurring; front-loaded floating provisioning muting QoQ profit (drew retail-investor pushback on optics/share price — mgmt defended as prudent).
- **NIM sustainability** at 2.5% global vs private-bank compression debate; growth optically lagging other PSUs due to balance-sheet clean-up.
- **Geopolitical / sector stress** (textile/chemical/steel) — none visible yet; SMA among lowest in years (2.9%).
bull_bear.title: Risks & watch-items

bull_bear.body: Confident, granular, guidance-forward MD (Ashok Chandra) who quantifies almost everything and repeatedly frames profitability + asset-quality + efficiency as the top agenda (built into field-staff KPIs). Strong, principled defence of quarterly ECL pre-provisioning against a retail investor's share-price complaint ("very, very prudent… someone has to take the hit"). Transparent on the low-yield run-off strategy and its optical drag on headline growth.
bull_bear.title: Management quality / tone

bull_bear.body:
- Headline advances +12.7% badly understates the business: core (ex-IBPC) is +15.4%, and management is *choosing* slower headline growth by shedding ~INR 57,000 cr of low-yield IBPC+corporate to protect NII/NIM.
- Gold-loan doubling isn't just growth — it's the mechanism to eliminate ~INR 900 cr/yr PSLC purchase cost and turn PNB into a PSLC *seller*, a direct cost-to-income lever.
- PNB is ahead of peers on ECL: it will enter 1-Apr-27 with the transition largely pre-funded (net ~INR 7-7.5k cr after floating), so the adoption should be a non-event vs banks provisioning it as a one-off shock.
- Fresh-underwriting quality proof point: INR 12.92 lakh cr disbursed over the last 6 years carries just INR 5,486 cr NPA (0.42%) — the post-clean-up book is very clean.
- IL&FS TN Power INR 1,000 cr write-back is a known FY27 profit "kitty" to be deployed in Q2/Q3.
bull_bear.title: Non-obvious takeaways

bull_bear.body:
- Capital at June'26: Total Capital (Tier 1+2) ₹166,377 Cr with CRAR 18.13%, Tier 1 ₹147,083 Cr (16.03%), Common Equity ₹133,285 Cr (CET-1 14.52%), Additional Tier 1 1.51% and Tier 2 2.10% — CET-1 up from 12.95% at June'25 while Tier 2 fell from 2.88%.
- Risk Weighted Assets ₹917,780 Cr at June'26 (Credit RWA ₹813,403 Cr, Market RWA ₹9,278 Cr, Operational RWA ₹95,099 Cr) versus ₹851,723 Cr at June'25.
- Book Value Per Share (Tangible) ₹108.58 at June'26 (+17.2% YoY) and Book Value Per Share (Total) ₹119.91; Return on Equity - Tangible 17.33% (annualized) in Q1 FY27.
- Group holdings retained: PNB Housing Finance Ltd 28.03%, PNB MetLife India Insurance 30%, PNB Gilts Ltd 74.07%, PNB Cards & Services and PNBISL at 100%, PNBIL London 100%, Druk PNB Bank Bhutan 51%, Everest Bank Nepal 20.02%, and 35% in each of eight RRBs.
bull_bear.title: Capital allocation policy (investor deck)

business.body:
- **Corporate book INR 5.15 lakh cr:** Infra 9%, Energy 4%, Roads/ports 4%, Food-processing 2%, Iron & steel ~2%, Metal products 1.8%. 86% of rated exposures >INR 25 cr are A+, 52% AAA.
- **Personal loans INR 23,727 cr — 100% salaried** (policy: no non-salaried PL). No stress from IT-sector/AI turmoil.
- **Gold loan** INR 31,888 cr (+103% YoY) — the standout growth + PSLC-gap lever.
- **Subsidiaries** (PNB Housing/MetLife/Gilts): no stake enhancement planned; focus on value maximisation, board interventions, PNB Housing new MD driving activity.

business.title: Challenges → beneficiaries & losers (listed names)

business.body:
- Scale as stated at June'26: Global Business ₹29,97,970 Cr (+10.2% YoY), Global Deposits ₹17,24,837 Cr (+8.5% YoY), Global Advances ₹12,73,132 Cr (+12.7% YoY), RAM Advances ₹6,88,487 Cr (+12.8% YoY).
- Ownership and rating: Govt. of India holds 70.08% of 1149.29 Crore shares; international ratings shown as BBB-/F3/Stable and Baa3/P-3/Stable; domestic Basel III ratings AA+ on Additional Tier-1 bonds and AAA on Tier-II bonds from four agencies.
- Asset-quality repair is the deck's central claim: GNPA% down from 4.98% (June'24) to 2.78% (June'26) and NNPA% from 0.60% to 0.28% over the same span, with PCR (incl. TWO) at 97.23% and PCR (excl. TWO) at 90.30%.
- Loan book skew stated as a strength: RAM share 57.2% of domestic advances at June'26 (56.6% a year earlier), with the domestic credit mix Retail 23.7%, Agriculture 16.6%, MSME 16.9% and Corporate & Others 42.8%.
- Credit quality of large exposures: in the >₹25 Crore externally rated standard portfolio, BBB & Above is 93.4% and BB & Below just 1.9% at June'26; in the NBFC book AAA & AA together comprise 98.63% of the total portfolio.
business.title: Positioning (investor deck)

business.body:
- [FY27 Guidance vs June'26 actuals] Credit growth 12%-13% vs 12.7%; Deposit growth 9%-10% vs 8.5%; CASA share 38% vs 36.7%; Operating profit growth 9%-10% vs 6.2%; NII growth 7% vs 2.1%; NIM 2.60%-2.70% vs 2.50%; GNPA <2.50% vs 2.78%; NNPA <0.3% vs 0.28%; PCR (incl. TWO) more than 96% vs 97.23%; Credit cost below 0.4% vs 0.25%; Total recovery >₹13,000 Crores vs ₹2,789 Crores; RoA above 1% vs 1.04%; Slippage ratio below 0.9% vs 0.68%.
- [Sector stress pockets] Despite headline GNPA of 2.78%, sector GNPA remains concentrated: Agriculture 9.07% and MSME 7.21% at June'26, versus Retail 0.75% and Corporate/Overseas/Others 0.09%; industry-wise, Food Processing 7.41% and Textiles 5.71% are the weakest.
- [NBFC concentration] NBFC exposure rose to ₹221,717 Cr at June'26 from ₹167,751 Cr at June'25, of which HFC ₹72,839 Cr, PSU and PSU-backed ₹50,609 Cr, Private ₹97,301 Cr and MFI ₹968 Cr.
- [RRB performance] Consolidated RRB position for June'26 (3M, unaudited): Business ₹271,319 Cr (+9.3%), Advances ₹105,061 Cr (+12.0%), Deposits ₹166,258 Cr (+7.7%), Capital Adequacy Ratio 14.58% (+99 bps) and Net profit ₹866 Cr (+77.7%).
- [Governance / innovation] PNB Quantum Innovation Hub set up for Quantum Computing and Quantum Analytics initiatives; ISO 9001:2015 certification obtained by key HO divisions; shortlisted for the RBI Regulatory Sandbox under the theme "Sustainable Finance and Climate Risk Mitigation".
business.title: Notable from the deck

latest_quarter.body:
- High-cost deposit repricing completed by May; PNB out of bulk-deposit & CD markets; cost of deposits −34 bps YoY. FCNR (CRR/SLR-exempt) to lower funding cost further.
- Cost-to-income 50.31% (from 55.31%) with clear 47-48% target — helped by falling PSLC purchase cost and AS-15 normalisation; NII/NIM up each quarter as low-yield tail runs off.
latest_quarter.title: Margins & cost dynamics

latest_quarter.body:
- **Q1 FY27 (this):** Business INR 29.98 lakh cr (+10.2% YoY); advances INR 12.73 lakh cr (+12.7% / +15.4% ex-IBPC), deposits INR 17.25 lakh cr (+8.5%). Net profit INR 5,253 cr; ROA 1.04%, ROE 17.33%; NII INR 10,798 cr (+4% QoQ); domestic NIM 2.64% (+3 bps), global 2.50%. GNPA 2.78% (−100 bps YoY), NNPA 0.28%, PCR 97.23%, slippage 0.68%; CRAR 18.13%, CET1 14.52%. Shed INR 22,411 cr IBPC + ~INR 35,000 cr sub-7% corporate. Gold loan INR 31,888 cr (+103%). C/I 50.31% (from 55.31%). Floating provision +INR 390 cr → INR 2,435 cr. Guidance: FCNR USD 2.5 bn (USD 425 mn done); GNPA<2.5%/NNPA<0.3%/PCR>96%/slippage<0.9%; C/I 47-48% by FY-end; gold loan INR 59-60k cr by FY-end; ECL one-time INR 9.5-10k cr + 10-12 bps/qtr; IL&FS TN Power INR 1,000 cr write-back Q2/Q3; treasury INR 900-1,000 cr/qtr; recovery INR 13,000 cr (INR 4,000 cr TWO); MSME ~25%; +INR 1 lakh cr digital sanctions; 250 branches; IT budget INR 3,400 cr; PSLC net-seller INR 5-10k cr next FY.
- _next Q → check: NIM QoQ step-up; FCNR-B toward USD 2.5 bn; gold-loan ramp toward INR 60k cr; C/I toward 47-48%; IL&FS write-back booked; ECL final digital calc (October); monsoon/El Niño agri impact; slippage/PCR vs guidance; IBPC fully run off._

outlook.body:
- **Growth / margin:** QoQ NIM improvement to continue every quarter as low-yield IBPC/corporate run off; on track to FY27 guidance; core RAM engines — retail +17.5%, MSME +19.8% (targeting ~25%), agri +16.4%; corporate +10%. Sanction pipeline INR 1.38 lakh cr pending disbursement.
- **Asset quality:** GNPA <2.5%, NNPA <0.3% (already 0.28%), PCR >96%, slippage ratio <0.9% (at 0.68%) — all FY27.
- **FCNR-B:** target **USD 2.5 billion**; USD 425 mn done (of which ~USD 200 mn via leverage); CRR/SLR-exempt → lowers cost of deposits over time.
- **Cost-to-income:** target **47-48% by FY27-end** (from 50.31%).
- **Gold loan:** grow to **INR 59,000-60,000 cr by FY27-end** (from INR 32,000 cr); 3,400 branches added (now ~6,400 doing gold).
- **PSLC:** next FY no purchase needed; aim to be a **net seller of INR 5,000-10,000 cr** (agri gold-loan +100% closing the priority-sector gap).
- **ECL (effective 1-Apr-2027):** one-time transition INR 9,500-10,000 cr (net of ~INR 2,435 cr floating ≈ INR 7,000-7,500 cr); ~10-12 bps/quarter recurring credit-cost impact; ample capital cushion.
- **IL&FS Tamil Nadu Power:** ~INR 1,000 cr excess provision to be written back in Q2/Q3 FY27 (all approvals in place).
- **Treasury income:** INR 900-1,000 cr per quarter outlook (INR 1,100 cr this quarter).
- **Recovery:** total INR 13,000 cr FY27 (of which ~INR 4,000 cr via technical-write-off route).
- **Network / capex:** 250 new branches (south + west focus); IT/digital budget ~INR 3,400 cr FY27; +INR 1 lakh cr cumulative digital-loan sanctions this year.
outlook.title: Guidance (CRITICAL — verify next quarter)

outlook.body:
- Q1 sanctions >INR 95,500 cr; INR 1.38 lakh cr pending disbursement → strong forward visibility.
- Digital credit sanctions INR 19,000+ cr in Q1; every 2nd loan now sanctioned digitally (was every 3rd); on track for +INR 1 lakh cr cumulative digital sanctions this FY.
- MSME driven by digital cash-flow-based lending + CGTMSE (75% cover); SIDBI-estimated INR 25-27 lakh cr sector credit gap = long runway.
outlook.title: Order book & pipeline (loan pipeline / growth drivers)

outlook.body:
- **Balance-sheet rejig** as an earnings lever: shedding sub-7% advances + IBPC and replacing with higher-yield RAM lifts NII/NIM even at modest headline growth.
- **Gold loan** doubling to close the PSLC gap and flip PNB from PSLC-buyer (INR ~900 cr cost) to seller — a structural cost-to-income tailwind.
- **Digital/AI/Quantum:** AI chatbots PIHU (customer) & RAHI (employee), GenAI credit-note & CRM tools; quantum-safe encryption on 86 customer-facing apps (NIST-certified), quantum mule-detection — efficiency + risk edge.
- Credit cards, cash-management, supply-chain finance flagged as emerging fee/diversification engines.
